meta.title: Task end notifications
meta.description: Shows a desktop notification when a chat turn ends, so you can work elsewhere while DeepSeek Harness runs. The notification names the conversation, its duration, the turn's token usage (input, output, and cache reads summed over the turn's model responses), and a short preview of the latest reply; a failed or interrupted turn says so in the title. Type /notify-test in the composer to send one test notification, which reports whether delivery succeeded. Windows raises a Windows toast under the DeepSeek Harness app identity and falls back to a tray balloon; if no notification appears, check that Windows notifications are allowed for DeepSeek Harness under Settings > System > Notifications, or set windowsChannel to balloon. macOS uses a notification banner; Linux uses notify-send. Only turns of interactive sessions notify — subagent children are skipped unless includeSubagents is enabled — and turns shorter than minDurationMs (3000 ms by default) are skipped. The plugin cannot tell whether the window is focused, so it notifies for every qualifying turn. Configuration is the Loader row, and no settings form is rendered: add an id-targeted entry to your profile's cordis.patch.yml with `id: task-notify`, `name: "@local/dsh-task-notify"` and the `config` fields you want; omitted fields keep their built-in defaults. Keys: enabled, notifyOnCompleted, notifyOnError, notifyOnAborted, minDurationMs, includeSubagents, previewChars, silent, titleCompleted, titleError, titleAborted, bodyTemplate (placeholders {session}, {duration}, {reason}, {tokens}; the default is `{session} · {duration} · {tokens}`, and dropping {tokens} hides token usage), windowsAppId, windowsChannel (auto, toast, balloon). The plugin only reads the session event feed and writes nothing to the session.
